surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was expected around $1.19 and within the $1.10–$1.30 guidance range, but Rogers reported $1.39, above even the guidance high end. That is a substantial upside gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS increased 54% year-over-year to $1.39, above the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted EPS was $1.19; Q3 guidance was $1.10–$1.30.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case put Q4 revenue at $235–245 million, with roughly $240 million implied by full-year consensus. Rogers guided to $215–225 million, a materially lower outlook, although the preview had identified a guide in this range as a downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 revenue guidance is $215–225 million, with a sequential decline on seasonality.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was Q4 guidance of $235–245 million and it flagged the guide against roughly $240 million implied by FY26 consensus; it also described $215–225 million as a possible downside case.

surprises.description: The preview expected roughly 5% annual organic growth, while management now expects about 9% organic growth in both Q3 and Q4. That is a faster near-term growth pace than the Investor Day target suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management now expects organic growth of about 9% in Q3 and Q4, running ahead of the approximately 5% annual organic growth target set at Investor Day.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the recent Investor Day growth plan and described the quarter as well-telegraphed, but did not anticipate organic growth running at about 9% in both Q3 and Q4.

surprises.description: The preview expected a first design-win checkpoint and revenue beginning in the second half of 2027. The call disclosed two sizable new wins, with one already starting a slow ramp in Q4 2026 and expected to reach full volume by Q2 2027; the call did not specify that these wins were data-center-related.
surprises.fact_evidence: Two sizable new design wins are expected to generate revenue in Q2–Q3 2027; one has begun a slow ramp in Q4 2026 and is expected to reach full volume by Q2 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had expected first AI data-center design wins within two quarters, with revenue starting in 2H 2027.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected at $238 million, exactly the guidance midpoint, but came in at $236.1 million. The shortfall was modest and management attributed it to supply constraints.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 sales rose 9% to $236.1 million, a couple of million dollars below the guidance midpoint due to supply constraints.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net sales were $238.0 million, exactly the $238 million guidance midpoint.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was close to the roughly $47 million expectation, but its margin reached 20.2%, above the approximately 19.8% expected. This also exceeded the preview’s anticipated year-over-year margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA grew 28% to $47.7 million, with margin expanding 300 basis points to 20.2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected approximately $47 million of adjusted EBITDA at an approximately 19.8% margin, with about 250 basis points of year-over-year margin expansion.

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected around 33.7%, but reached 34.2%, the top of the company’s guidance range. This was a better result than the consensus midpoint, despite rising commodity costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin reached 34.2%, up 70 basis points year-over-year, driven by higher volume and mix and partially offset by rising commodity costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put consensus gross margin at about 33.7% and noted a guidance range of 33.2%–34.2%.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the balance sheet and free cash flow but did not anticipate a quarterly share repurchase. Rogers bought back $9.3 million of shares while cash and short-term investments still increased by $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased $9.3 million of shares in Q3 and grew cash and short-term investments by $25 million to $236.4 million, with free cash flow of $35.4 million.
